recheck.text: What the endpoint answers for a malformed request: no `assignee` field, a non-string non-null value (a number, an object, an array), extra unknown fields, a body that is not a JSON object, a body that is not valid JSON or not valid UTF-8, and an unknown ticket id.

Whether the documentation and release records describe the change: docs/api.md (endpoint, ticket field, filter, audit action, notification), README command-line columns, a CHANGELOG.md section with a version bump in package.json, and a decision record if a format or rule changed.

defects.title: An agent name holding invalid UTF-8 is accepted and stored altered
defects.repro: Start the service; POST /tickets {"title":"Printer jam","priority":"low","requester":"ann@example.com"}; send PUT /tickets/T-0001/assignee with Content-Type application/json and the raw body bytes 7B 22 61 73 73 69 67 6E 65 65 22 3A 22 64 61 FF 6E 61 22 7D ({"assignee":"da<0xFF>na"}); GET /tickets/T-0001.
defects.observed: 200; assignee is "da�na" (U+FFFD replacing the byte); an audit entry and a notification to that altered name are queued.
defects.expected: 400 invalid (the body is not valid UTF-8), the ticket, audit and outbox unchanged.

defects.title: No CHANGELOG.md section and no version bump for the assignment feature
defects.repro: Compare CHANGELOG.md and package.json of the delivered tree with the starting files
defects.observed: both identical to the starting files: top changelog section is 1.4.0 (2025-09-15), version 1.4.0
defects.expected: a new changelog section describing assignment and a bumped version (inventory U-22)

defects.title: An agent named '-' is indistinguishable from an unassigned ticket in the command line
defects.repro: POST /tickets {...}; PUT /tickets/T-0001/assignee {"assignee":"-"} -> 200; stop; node bin/tickets.js --data FILE list and show T-0001
defects.observed: ASSIGNEE column and show's assignee line print '-', the same marker used for unassigned tickets
defects.expected: either refuse '-' as a name or show unassigned with a marker no accepted name can take, so the two are distinguishable

defects.title: Assignee with an invalid UTF-8 byte is accepted and stored with a replacement character
defects.repro: printf '{"assignee":"da\xffna"}' > b.json; curl -X PUT -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary @b.json http://HOST/tickets/T-0001/assignee
defects.observed: 200, assignee 'da\ufffdna', audit entry and a notification to that name (inherited body parsing: titles behave the same)
